desc: Implement the min-heap boundary expansion solution: initialize heap with start's neighbors, repeatedly absorb the smallest boundary cell while `X*S < current_strength`, push newly exposed neighbors, using Python ints and the strict inequality.
Verify against all three provided samples (expect 28, 5, 1343); worker confirmed all pass.
Check edge cases: no absorbable neighbors, X = 1, single-cell grid, duplicate heap entries skipped via occupied check, and large sums (Python big ints handle 10^21).

Confirm greedy correctness: `current_strength` only increases and the boundary only grows, so absorbing any legal boundary cell can never hurt the final result; the min-keyed break is valid because if the smallest boundary cell fails, all larger ones fail too.
Complexity is O(HW log(HW)) time and O(HW) memory, within limits for H,W ≤ 500.
